cards.text: Zechariah is a prophet to God's people, and they're rebuilding the house of God in Jerusalem (Zechariah 1:1; Ezra 5:1-2). He's just watched four chariots ride out in a vision, and now the word of the LORD comes to him again. No horses this time, friend. Just a TO-DO LIST.
Step one: take an offering from three exiles who just got in from Babylon, Heldai, Tobijah and Jedaiah. These guys haven't even UNPACKED yet, and the prophet's already at the door for the offering.

cards.question: Zechariah's next stop is the house of Josiah son of Zephaniah. True or false: God tells him to go there that same day.

cards.text: Next, God tells Zechariah to take silver and gold and make something ornate. Me? I spent YEARS under takeout menus in a junk drawer, and NOBODY ever called me ornate.

cards.question: God's plan for that silver and gold: make an ornate ___.
The ornate silver and gold crown is ready. Whose head does Zechariah set it on?

cards.text: So the crown goes on Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest. Then Zechariah is to tell him what the LORD of Hosts says: 'Here is a man whose name is the Branch, and He will branch out from His place…'

cards.question: God's people are rebuilding right now. So what will the man called the Branch do? He will build the ___ of the LORD.

cards.text: Then it comes AGAIN: 'Yes, He will build the temple of the LORD; He will be clothed in splendor and will sit on His throne and rule.' When I say something twice, it's because I forgot I said it. When God says it twice, friend, you LEAN IN.

cards.question: The Branch will sit on His throne and rule. What else will He be, right there on that throne?
A ruler and a priest, all on one throne. Fill it in: there will be ___ counsel between the two.

cards.text: The crown becomes a memorial to Helem, Tobijah, Jedaiah and the gracious son of Zephaniah. The Millers carved MY name into my handle, and these folks get remembered with a CROWN. Same idea. WAY shinier.

cards.question: That memorial crown has to live somewhere. Where does it stay?

answers.text: In the temple of the LORD

cards.text: Then the picture gets BIGGER than this little crowd at Josiah's house. It's like you plan a small get-together, and suddenly the guest list is your WHOLE PHONE.

cards.question: True or false: only the people already there will come and build the temple of the LORD.

cards.text: And when it happens, here's the line: 'you will know that the LORD of Hosts has sent Me to you.' But hold up, friend. There's an IF.

cards.question: All this about the temple and those far away comes with a condition. What is it?

answers.text: If they diligently obey the LORD's voice
If they finish the city walls first
If they bring more silver and gold

findings.problem: The opening card has 4 sentences: 'Zechariah is a prophet…', 'He's just watched four chariots…', 'No horses this time, friend.' and 'Just a TO-DO LIST.' The limit is 3.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences.

findings.problem: The card states a Bible fact from outside the passage, that Zechariah just saw four chariots ride out in a vision, but gives no reference for it (Zechariah 6:1-8). The other outside facts on this card do have references.

rule.text: Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: The joke stresses how fast things are moving: the exiles 'haven't even UNPACKED yet' and the prophet is 'already at the door.' This hints that the answer to card 3 (go that same day) is True, and points the baker away from False.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences: the quote, 'When I say something twice…' and 'When God says it twice…'.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The question says 'A ruler and a priest, all on one throne' and then refers to 'the two.' This decides who 'the two' in verse 13 are. The text doesn't say who they are, or how the throne and the priest connect.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: This story card has 4 sentences: 'The crown becomes a memorial…', 'The Millers carved MY name…', 'Same idea.' and 'WAY shinier.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The card says the picture gets bigger than the people at Josiah's house and compares it to a guest list that grows to the whole phone. This tells the baker the answer to card 15 (False: people beyond those present will come) before they answer it.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: 'The people already there' points back to the 'little crowd at Josiah's house' on card 14, which is no longer on screen. The question doesn't say who these people are or where 'there' is.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences: the quote, 'But hold up, friend.' and 'There's an IF.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The card quotes 'you will know that the LORD of Hosts has sent Me to you' but doesn't say who 'Me' is. The rule says to name the speaker before an 'I' quote. The text doesn't make clear whether 'Me' is Zechariah or another messenger, and the rule also says to leave open what the text leaves open.
findings.question: When a quote uses 'I' or 'Me' and the text doesn't say who is speaking, should Papa Dorin name the most likely speaker (here, the prophet, as in Zechariah 2:9 and 4:9), or keep the speaker open with a neutral lead-in like 'here's the line'?

findings.problem: The right answer, 'If they diligently obey the LORD's voice,' is the only spiritual answer and the only one with biblical wording ('diligently'). The wrong answers are practical tasks. The right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.
